title: Garbage Collector
blurb: Refcounting beside mark-and-sweep on the same heap. Refcounting leaks 1, 2, 5 and 2 on the cycle cases.
expected:
--- trees: both collectors agree ---
live tree: 4 allocated, refcount freed 0, mark-sweep freed 0
    refcount left:   [leaf, left, right, root]
    mark-sweep left: [leaf, left, right, root]
dropped tree: 4 allocated, refcount freed 4, mark-sweep freed 4
    refcount left:   []
    mark-sweep left: []
--- sharing ---
two roots: 3 allocated, refcount freed 0, mark-sweep freed 0
    refcount left:   [root-1, root-2, shared]
    mark-sweep left: [root-1, root-2, shared]
one root dropped: 3 allocated, refcount freed 1, mark-sweep freed 1
    refcount left:   [root-2, shared]
    mark-sweep left: [root-2, shared]
both dropped: 3 allocated, refcount freed 3, mark-sweep freed 3
    refcount left:   []
    mark-sweep left: []
--- cycles: where refcounting loses ---
self cycle: 2 allocated, refcount freed 0, mark-sweep freed 1  <- refcounting leaked 1
    refcount left:   [live, self-cycle]
    mark-sweep left: [live]
two-node cycle: 3 allocated, refcount freed 0, mark-sweep freed 2  <- refcounting leaked 2
    refcount left:   [cycle-a, cycle-b, keep]
    mark-sweep left: [keep]
five-node ring: 6 allocated, refcount freed 0, mark-sweep freed 5  <- refcounting leaked 5
    refcount left:   [keep, ring0, ring1, ring2, ring3, ring4]
    mark-sweep left: [keep]
garbage cycle beside live data: 4 allocated, refcount freed 0, mark-sweep freed 2  <- refcounting leaked 2
    refcount left:   [garbage-a, garbage-b, kept, root]
    mark-sweep left: [kept, root]
--- the summary ---
Reference counting freed everything mark-and-sweep did, except a cycle.
That is the whole difference between the two algorithms, and it is why
Grasm's own `ref` is generational rather than counted: a generation
check catches a stale handle without needing to know whether anything
still points at the slot ([T-REF-GENERATIONAL]).
